payload.title: quiet-items: a tracker write drew in full with both mods on, once, beside an auto mode classifier note

payload.text: Live check 2026-10-08, Claude Code 2.1.295, quiet-items 0.3.1, simple-view 0.1.2, scratch br repo, auto mode. 4 br writes with both mods on: 3 drew one quiet row (br update live-ek2 --priority 1 and 2; br update live-j32 with quiet off drew a simple row as expected). 1 (br update live-ek2 --status in_progress, the first write after /quiet-items turned on) drew the engine full row with the whole issues.jsonl diff and the line 'Allowed by auto mode classifier'. A toggle off and on before a write did not reproduce it, so the toggle is ruled out. The classifier is a candidate with one observation; the cause is unknown.

Code reading 2026-10-08 (no live test): no certain path. Best fit, unproven: a race inside one draw. quiet-items' render hook reads rows while empty and passes (mods/quiet-items/hooks/register.tsx:194-199); its rows write lands (register.tsx:141); simple-view then reads rows filled and also passes (mods/simple-view/hooks/register.ts:257-260, 347), so both ToolUse and ToolResult draw as the engine draws them. Needs the engine to draw before quiet-items' tool.call returns and a missed redraw. Second candidate: quiet-items stores no rows and simple-view rejects the stored output (output.ts:100-101). The classifier note is likely on every engine row in auto mode, hidden when a mod draws. Probe: repeat br update until a full row appears, then run /simple twice to force a redraw: the race turns into the quiet row, the second candidate stays an engine row; /simple show 1 then shows the stored output shape.

Live probe 2026-10-09, Claude Code 2.1.295, mods from main 4df7be1 (workitems, quiet-items 0.3.1, simple-view 0.1.2), scratch br repo, auto mode, both mods on: 12 of 12 br update calls drew one quiet row, in 2 rounds (8 writes after both toggles; 4 writes right after /quiet-items off and on). No full row appeared, so the race and the second candidate stay unproven. Total sightings: 1 full row in 16 writes.

2026-10-14 live check, Claude Code 2.1.300, mods from main (quiet-items 0.5.0, simple-view 0.5.1), scratch br repo, auto mode: /quiet-items off, /quiet-items on, then 4 br update calls, the first right after the toggle as in the sighting. All 4 drew one quiet row (work item updated ...). Total since the single sighting on 2.1.295: 16 of 16 quiet rows.

## Trigger

When I scan the file tree for changed files, I want the name itself coloured by its state with the mark right beside it, so I can see added, edited and deleted files at a glance.

Person request 2026-10-28 after using handily-filetree 0.2.0: the yellow-orange M in a far right column is not the wanted look. ## Context

Owner rule of 2026-11-16, given in the basicly window and relayed by the Orchestrator: "5 minutes is the max for CI. and for all release related preps and checks another 5 min max. normal CI build 5 min, release CI build 10 mins. ## Trigger

When my terminal uses a Nerd Font Mono font, I want handily to draw icons for task states, git states, file types, agents and toast kinds, so I can read the mods at a glance; on any other terminal the plain marks stay.

## Evidence

Person request 2026-10-27, approved the same day: use Nerd Fonts for better visualization. A mod cannot choose or install a font; Nerd Font icons are Unicode private-use characters that render only with a Nerd Font. nerd-fonts readme (fetched 2026-10-27): the plain patched font draws icons double width by default, Mono draws them single width, Propo proportional. handily counts a private-use character as 1 column, gated in every mod by scripts/width.test.mjs, so only Mono keeps rows aligned. Plan: one glyph table with sets plain and nerd, each code point pinned and gated like width.ts; a bundle setting glyphs plain or nerd; a /handily glyphs test line; a designer drafts the icon set and mocks first. Starts after the toast and filetree epics so their marks are final. Depends on the terminal project: the person asked the terminal improvements session on 2026-10-27 to set up a Nerd Font Mono terminal font; the live test waits for that.

## Scope

mods/*/hooks glyph copies, mods/handily, scripts, docs/mocks.md, docs/design.md

payload.text: Depends on term-uy9muk in the terminal tracker (filed 2026-10-27 by the terminal improvements session): draw Nerd Font icons at single width. The terminal WezTerm config already uses the bundled Symbols Nerd Font Mono fallback (terminal_setup/templates/wezterm.lua:236-240), so WezTerm may draw icons in one cell with no font install; Windows Terminal, PowerShell and Git Bash windows outside WezTerm are not covered. The live glyph test waits for term-uy9muk.

term-uy9muk closed 2026-10-27 by the terminal improvements session: in WezTerm, U+F07B draws from the bundled Symbols Nerd Font Mono with cells=1 on Windows and in WSL, measured with wezterm ls-fonts; the main font stays Cascadia Mono or DejaVu Sans Mono; the icon glyph is slightly wider than its cell but the next character does not move. The VS Code terminal and Windows Terminal are not covered and may show empty boxes, so the glyph set stays opt-in. The terminal repo tests both facts and documents the check command. The glyph design can start.

docs/mocks.md gains section 11 with the approved glyph mocks and the stand-in legend, and the signals table in docs/design.md has a Nerd column that scripts/signals.test.mjs checks.

payload.text: Three pre-commit refusals on 2026-11-12 in the switch lane, each in handily-reply-view, each a different test. The last: c4.test.ts, the C4Context example at 80 columns, took 1682.74 ms of 5000 ms, a third is about 1667 ms, machine factor 1.01. The run held no foreign load. Retrying passes. Fix the cost of the tests or declare their limit, never weaken the gate.

Measured 2026-11-12 (scratchpad speed-spread.py over claude plugin test mods/handily-reply-view, generated.test.ts left out because it declares its own limits; limit third 1666.67 ms). Quiet, runs 8 to 17 after the basicly repack ended: 9 of 10 runs had no test over a third, sum of test times 476 to 511 s; run 11 had 8 tests over and a sum of 659 s, cause unknown. Loaded, 10 runs with claude plugin test mods/handily-board started beside each run: 5 of 10 runs had 1 to 3 tests over, sum 539 to 591 s (+12 percent). The slowest quiet tests have medians of 916 to 1202 ms; the C4Context test median 1202, max 1406 quiet and 1572 loaded, 1682 in the refused commit. So the tests are not slow on a quiet machine; the spread comes from load. Pre-commit runs its 5 checks in parallel (check_execution.py _run_parallel) and each mod runs about 30 test files at once on 32 cores. machineSlowness reads its reference tests from handily-board while board runs, so it does not see the load during the reply-view run. Fix in how the gate measures, not a higher limit.

Decided by the orchestrator, 2026-11-12: option (a). The gate measured the machine, not the test; a re-run alone measures what the limit is about, so this corrects the measurement and does not weaken the gate. Conditions: the limit does not change; one re-run, alone, after the suite; a test still over fails the commit; output prints the first time, the re-run time and the load for each re-run test, also when it passes; creep must show through a count of re-runs per test and a warning share of the limit; tests for over-only-first passes, over-both fails, limit unchanged; report the share of the C4Context test and file a record if above the warning share. Start as the third lane when one frees.
